Subject: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (hosted vs reserved vs VPC)

Hi Alicia — great talk earlier, thanks for walking through Vertis' ingestion profile. Short recap and the two asks we promised to follow up on: a) simple cost comparison (hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved commits) for your baseline workload, and b) feasibility + rough pricing for a Private VPC (data residency + SOC2 + on-prem gateway).

Key signals from the call that I summarized:
- Estimated steady-state: ~200M inference calls / month, average prompt+response ~450 tokens, peak hour ~20% of daily volume.
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 150ms for short-form responses; some long requests (multi-turn) can tolerate higher P95.
- Data: US-only tenancy, SOC2 + annual penetration test required.
- Procurement: 60–90 day procurement window; decision likely tied to both cost (TCO) and data controls.

Attached: vertis_usage_snapshot.csv (export of the telemetry you shared). I also attached a one-pager with a pilot term sheet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal costing note (Karthik): high-level per-token hosted estimate + two reserved commit scenarios (6mo pilot commit, 12mo commit) — deliver by EOD Monday.
2) Tech due-diligence: Monica to lead a short security questionnaire + VPC topology options; will follow up with a SOC2 evidence list.
3) Pricing workshop: 30m sync next week to walk the numbers and choose pilot structure.

If that matches your expectation, I can send a calendar invite for Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — this is perfect. A couple of clarifications to make sure the modeling aligns:
- The 200M calls figure is aggregate for two services we run; the smaller internal service (~30M) can tolerate higher latency and could be a good candidate for Dedicated, while the user-facing service (~170M) needs the P95 target.
- We have an internal procurement cap of $120k/month for infra unless we can show net TCO savings over 12 months for a commit.
- On the VPC: our security team will want to see encryption-at-rest key ownership (KMS/HSM) and the option for an on-prem proxy (air-gapped) for sensitive payloads.

Can Karthik include both a straight per-token hosted scenario and a blended run-rate that assumes 60% of traffic on a dedicated pool (reserved) and 40% on hosted (burst/fallback)? That will help us compare with internal finance expectations.

Also Tom from ScalerCloud is on the thread as they're our infra partner evaluating network/connectivity options for a VPC/on-prem routing. He may have quick questions about egress models.

Appreciate it —
Alicia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 7 May 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick recap + numbers we discussed (hosted vs reserved vs VPC)

Alicia / team — I put together a short costing sheet and three scenarios; link below. High-level numbers here are illustrative (rounded):

1) Hosted-only (per-token)
- List price: $0.0035 per input+output token average (volume tiers apply)
- For 200M calls * 450 tokens = 90B tokens / month -> approx $315k / month list -> tiering/commit discounts can reduce this to ~$210k/mo at your volume assumptions.

2) Dedicated reserved (6mo pilot commit)
- Recommended pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed throughput) -> reserved billing ~ $110k / month + token egress/overage allowances -> effective unit economics equivalent to ~$0.0017 per token at steady utilization (70% effective). Upfront: 6-month minimum billing; we can structure a pilot credit against the first two months to de-risk.

3) Private VPC / On-prem gateway
- Base: platform license + infra pass-through. One-time onboarding + secure network link: ~$85k engineering & onboarding estimate, then infra OPEX (you manage compute or we run in a VPC with pass-through charges). For sensitive workloads this is ideal for compliance but has higher upfront cost; break-even vs hosted-only is around 9–14 months depending on utilization.

Blended scenario (your ask): 60% Dedicated + 40% Hosted -> modeled at ~$140k / month (combined) vs hosted-only ~$210k/mo (discounted). This assumes you can route the high-SLA traffic to Dedicated and burst to Hosted for spikes.

Spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcDEF-vertis-cost-model
Pilot term sheet (attached): redwood-pilot-term-sheet.pdf

Open items I haven't fully priced: egress networking for the VPC (Tom can chime in), and exact quantization/latency tradeoffs for your model family (we can run a short perf test).

If helpful, I can convert the numbers into a 12-month TCO table for your finance team.

—Karthik
